Subject: SIG follow-up: VPC peering / private endpoint evidence request

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this — Atlas Health is completing the SIG questionnaire and we hit a few questions in the network/security section that need concrete evidence. Our security team specifically asked for:

- Walkthrough of how Redwood supports private connectivity (VPC peering vs PrivateLink).
- Exact IP ranges to allowlist for egress and any managed endpoints.
- Evidence of peering acceptance (screenshots or IDs) and a sample of VPC Flow Logs showing traffic to your endpoints.
- Clarification on whether TLS is terminated in your control plane and if source IP is preserved for our allowlist rules.

Can you share a short package (docs/screenshots/CSV of CIDRs) we can attach to the SIG? We need this by EOD Thursday to keep the onboarding timeline.

Regards,
Alice Burns

alice.burns@atlashealth.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: VPC peering / private endpoint evidence request

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Quick ack: we can deliver the package and a short narrative for the SIG. What I will provide in this message (and attach):

- A CSV with the IPv4 CIDRs we publish for hosted egress and control-plane endpoints (vpc-allowlist-ips.csv).
- A snapshot showing a peering acceptance record (vpc-peering-acceptance-snapshot.png) from our account for a previous Dedicated customer as a template.
- Sample VPC Flow Logs with timestamps redacted (flowlogs-sample.txt).
- Network diagram showing both Hosted + Dedicated topologies (redwood-network-diagram.pdf).

Short answers inline to your bullets:
- Private connectivity: for our hosted (multi-tenant) product we provide private endpoints (AWS PrivateLink / Azure Private Link) for control-plane traffic; we do not require customers to peer into Redwood VPCs. For Dedicated / Private deployments we support both VPC peering (cross-account) and PrivateLink depending on customer preference and routing constraints.
- IP ranges: attached CSV contains stable prefix lists for control-plane endpoints and known egress ranges. These are updated through drive links and we version them.
- Evidence: I attached a peering acceptance snapshot and a sanitized flow log sample. For production sign-off we can provide a real-time console screenshot or a peering ID (redacted in this thread) under an NDA.
- TLS termination / source IP: TLS to our control plane is terminated at our edge (Cloud Load Balancer) with TLS 1.2+; for PrivateLink traffic TLS stays on the customer side until the interface endpoint — application TLS termination is up to the deployment model. Source IP preservation: for PrivateLink and cross-account peering the original source IP is preserved; when traffic traverses our NAT egress for hosted customers, source IP will be a Redwood-managed NAT IP (hence we recommend allowlisting the published egress CIDRs).

I'll follow up shortly with the attachments. If you need an acceptance ID to reference in the SIG, let me know and we can provide an obfuscated ID plus the Redacted Customer Acceptance screenshot under an MSA.

—Olga
Olga Petrov

Hi Alice — attaching the evidence bundle and a short narrative you can paste into the SIG responses. Drive link and artifacts below.

Key points (summary for SIG):
1) Connectivity options
   - Hosted API: recommended path is PrivateLink interface endpoints for control plane and management traffic; no cross-account peering required.
   - Dedicated / Private: supported via cross-account VPC peering (we provide peering parameters and accept the connection), or via PrivateLink where customers prefer managed endpoints.

2) Allowlist guidance
   - For hosted customers who must allowlist egress: allowlist the Redwood egress CIDR set in vpc-allowlist-ips.csv.
   - For PrivateLink: allowlist the ENI/endpoint IPs provided during onboarding (these are in the enrollment payload).

3) Source IP and TLS
   - PrivateLink and Peering: source IP preserved; TLS can be end-to-end depending on your TLS model.
   - Hosted (public path through our edge): TLS terminated at our load balancer; for source-ip preservation we recommend allowlisting Redwood egress ranges.

4) Evidence provided (attached):
   - vpc-allowlist-ips.csv — current published CIDRs (version 2027-03-01).
   - vpc-peering-acceptance-snapshot.png — sample console screenshot (sanitized).
   - flowlogs-sample.txt — redacted VPC Flow Logs showing accepted traffic to PrivateLink endpoint.
   - redwood-network-diagram.pdf — diagram showing Hosted vs Dedicated topology and where PrivateLink/peering sit.

5) Next steps / actions we can take for Atlas Health
   - If you want cross-account peering, provide the requester account ID and VPC CIDR; we will open and accept the peering and provide the peering connection ID.
   - If you prefer PrivateLink, request the interface endpoint during onboarding and we will return the endpoint service name and example CloudFormation template.

Thanks Olga — the artifacts are excellent and will plug straight into the SIG. A couple of clarifying questions from our infra team:

1) For PrivateLink, are the interface endpoint IPs static per region or do they change across deployments? We need to know whether we can allowlist a stable prefix or must accept per-endpoint IPs for each onboarding.
2) For cross-account peering: do you accept peering connections from AWS accounts that have overlapping secondary CIDRs (we use secondary ranges for namespaces)? If not, what is your recommendation?
3) For hosted customers, if we rely on your egress CIDRs, what is the SLA/process if you rotate those ranges — how much lead time do you provide?

If you can answer these succinctly we can close the SIG checklist.

Alice

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: VPC peering / private endpoint evidence request

Hi Alice — quick answers to the infra questions below: 

1) PrivateLink endpoint IPs: interface endpoint ENI addresses are allocated in your customer VPC and therefore are per-deployment and per-region; they are not part of a single stable Redwood-owned prefix. For that reason we provide two options:
   a) Best when possible: create interface endpoints in your VPC and allowlist the endpoint ENIs that appear in your account during onboarding (these are static for the endpoint lifecycle).
   b) If you need a stable prefix: use our published egress CIDR set and route traffic through a customer NAT or BASTION that you control; or use Transit Gateway with prefix advertising — we can work with your network team to establish a stable advertisement pattern.

2) Cross-account peering and overlapping secondary CIDRs: AWS does not allow peering when the primary CIDR blocks overlap. For secondary ranges that overlap we ask for the full CIDR set during onboarding; if overlap exists we recommend either:
   - Using PrivateLink instead (avoids peering restrictions), or
   - Re-assigning non-overlapping secondary ranges for the pair of VPCs to be peered, or
   - Using a Transit Gateway and NAT-based routing where appropriate. Hannah and I can run a quick validation if you share the proposed CIDRs.

3) Egress CIDR rotation and lead time: we maintain a published CIDR set with versioning. Typical rotation windows are 30 days notice for non-emergency changes. For emergency security rotations we notify customers via the Console and the registered security contact and provide an expedited onboarding window. We can include a signed attestation of our notification process in the SIG if that helps.

Next steps:
- If you want us to validate CIDRs, reply with the (sanitized) list and we will run a compatibility check and open NET-1247 to track.
- If you prefer PrivateLink, confirm region(s) and we will provide a sample CloudFormation template and the onboarding playbook.

I'll update the SIG portal with these clarifications and attach the artifacts once you confirm.

Thanks — Olga
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
